subject: RiverLake Health - Private/VPC discovery recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@riverlakehealth.org>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: RiverLake Health - Private/VPC discovery recap

Hi Alice—

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure we captured requirements correctly and align on next steps. If anything below looks off, please flag.

Key pain points discussed:
- Regulated PHI workloads: must be HIPAA-compliant with auditable access logs and strong separation between environments.
- Network constraints: primary inference cluster needs to sit in an internal VPC with no outbound internet egress; occasional limited egress for OS/security patching is okay under controlled windows.
- Customer-managed keys: requirement to integrate with existing HSM/KMS (Thales/HSM + AWS KMS) and ensure keys never leave customer control.
- Air-gap scenario: some facilities may require an air-gapped deployment for local inference where updates are delivered via signed media.

Current stack you described:
- Core EHR + analytics in GCP (us-central)
- On-prem data lake in Prod VLANs for sensitive PHI
- Existing IAM via Okta and centralized logging to Splunk

Success criteria for pilot / PoC:
- Private deployment in customer VPC with no public egress during normal operations
- KMS/HSM integration demonstrated (key wrap/unwrap flow + no-key-export proof points)
- End-to-end audit log capture to your Splunk instance
- Latency target: p95 inference < 450ms for 512-token requests for our initial test set
- Security review passed (SOC2 artifacts + architecture diagrams)

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with RiverLake infra + security (90 min) — propose Tue/Thu next week.
2) Share our SOC2 artifact package and a short runbook for KMS integrations (attached).
3) If deep-dive looks good, scope a 4-week PoC with a single VPC and one-region private control plane.

Attachments: network_topology.pdf (network diagram stub), soc2_overview.pdf (SOC2 artifact stub)

Thanks — I'll follow up with proposed time slots for the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 15, 2026 at 3:02 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

> 
> Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure we captured requirements correctly and align on next steps. If anything below looks off, please flag.
> 
> Key pain points discussed:
> - Regulated PHI workloads: must be HIPAA-compliant with auditable access logs and strong separation between environments.
> - Network constraints: primary inference cluster needs to sit in an internal VPC with no outbound internet egress; occasional limited egress for OS/security patching is okay under controlled windows.
> - Customer-managed keys: requirement to integrate with existing HSM/KMS (Thales/HSM + AWS KMS) and ensure keys never leave customer control.
> - Air-gap scenario: some facilities may require an air-gapped deployment for local inference where updates are delivered via signed media.

Thanks — this is accurate and very helpful. A few clarifications / asks from our side:
- Egress: zero outbound by default. We can allow scheduled egress windows for patching but need to validate how Redwood handles pipeline updates without internet (signed bundles + offline install process).
- KMS: we use a Thales HSM in the datacenter and AWS KMS for cloud workloads. We need an architecture that supports both and allows key rotation under our control.
- Logging: Splunk is our source of truth — will need a connector or log-forwarding approach (S3 bucket + forwarder or direct syslog).
- Compliance artifacts: please include encryption-at-rest diagrams and data-flow mapping for PHI in the SOC2 package.

Timeline: target internal review by 7/10. If we can run the technical deep-dive this week or early next, that helps our timeline.

I'm looped in our procurement alias above for initial pricing and SOW questions.

— Alice
Alice Johnson
Director, IT Security | RiverLake Health
alice.johnson@riverlakehealth.org
+1 (617) 555-2299

Thanks Alice— glad that matches. A few quick confirms and next steps from our side: 

- Egress / air-gap: we support signed update bundles for air-gapped installs. I'll have Aditya share the offline update runbook and our checksum/signature process during the deep-dive.
- KMS/HSM: Dev will walk through both our cloud KMS plugin and an on-prem HSM integration pattern (key-wrap approach; keys never exported).
- Logging: we can forward audit logs to an S3 endpoint or stream to Splunk — Dev will cover the config options.
- SOC2 & encryption diagrams: attaching the SOC2 overview now; we'll add a short data-flow diagram and an encryption-at-rest schematic ahead of the deep-dive.

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive (90 min):
- Wed 6/17 10:00-11:30 PT
- Thu 6/18 14:00-15:30 PT
- Fri 6/19 09:00-10:30 PT

Aditya / Dev — can you confirm availability for any of these slots? I'll send an invite (tech_deepdive-schedule.ics attached) once Alice confirms a preferred slot.

Next deliverables (we'll send before the deep-dive):
- Offline update runbook (Aditya)
- HSM/KMS integration notes + key-wrap demo plan (Dev)
- Expanded SOC2/data-flow diagram (Marissa)

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
